Chapter 9: Thomas—Honest Doubt and Unshakable Faith.
You’ve probably heard of Thomas as the disciple who doubted, but his story is so much more than just a single moment of hesitation. Picture him as a realist, someone who just couldn’t take things on faith alone—he needed to see with his own eyes before he could believe. So when the word spread that their teacher had returned, Thomas didn’t just nod along. He wanted proof, not just wishful thinking.
Now, most of us in his shoes might’ve kept quiet, afraid of what others would think. Not Thomas. He put his doubts right out there for everyone to hear—even if it meant risking being misunderstood. And when he finally got the chance to see for himself—to actually touch and know—it wasn’t cynicism that came out, but pure awe. “My Lord and my God.” Just imagine the relief and reverence in those words.
What’s amazing is that Thomas’s honesty didn’t just help him—it became a gift to everyone around him. By speaking up, he made it easier for others to admit their own questions and uncertainties. And over time, Thomas transformed. He became a person of deep, unwavering conviction. Tradition says he even journeyed far from home, bringing hope to distant places, facing real dangers along the way. His faith, once fragile, turned truly unshakable.
So if you’ve ever struggled with doubts, Thomas’s journey is a gentle reminder—it’s okay to ask, to wonder, to seek out your own answers. The best kind of faith doesn’t shy away from honest questions. In fact, it grows even stronger because of them.
